questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Arbitrates'**

 [IMAGE: https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/Jzuzw-8wuBgigTndMhoY-ZAI4VWmag98opLmt6A2ZHz_5cExJUQJakb7b2-_MWACOaqYofpEwx4p1izSVwzvEnEG9O-qNRtSHH5fMhiXmRUrMAk6dGo9yQCfIBg1xBNfMrwkPgoK] Explanation: 

__
 
• From the given options, only the word 'Arbitrates' is making any sense or is meaningful.
 
• The word 'Arbitrates' means to give an opinion about (something at issue or in dispute).
 
• It is in the simple present tense to indicate a general rule or a regular occurrence
 
• The **synonyms** of the word '**arbitrates**' are "**adjudge, adjudicate, decide, determine, judge, referee, rule (on), settle, umpire**".
 
• The **antonyms** of the word '**arbitrates**' are "**equivocate, hedge, pussyfoot, skirt**".
 
• **Hence**, the option '**arbitrates**' is the correctly spelt word.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8d299c1f8ac17c3d0f55c88318dc051a9a17b579eb18127685f8613e4a4990a.png] Extra- Bites- 

 
• **Examples** of '**arbitrates**' in a **sentence**__:

 
 
• *The supreme court, which **arbitrates** on constitutional disputes but has not ruled against the government since 2003.*
 
• *The State Council **arbitrates** in disputed administrative matters and gives advice on all bills and decrees.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

What seeds you (has sow) in the garden of your mind determine the quality of life you shall have.
questions.solution: The clue “determine” says that it is in present tense. So “sowing” is inappropriate here. Likewise “had sow” is both grammatically invalid and in past tense. We say “as you sow so shall you reap.” Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Opening the door to her each morning is like (lets) a breath of fresh air into my world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Letting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, "letting" functions as a **gerund**, which is a verb form that acts as a noun.
 
• Gerunds are formed by adding -ing to a verb and can be used as subjects, objects, or complements in a sentence.
 
• In the sentence "Opening the door to her each morning is like letting a breath of fresh air into my world," "letting" is a gerund functioning as the direct object of the verb "is like."
 
• The gerund phrase "letting a breath of fresh air into my world" is the object of comparison and is equivalent to "the act of letting a breath of fresh air into my world." It describes the action or process that is being compared to the act of opening the door.
 
• The gerund form "letting" is grammatically appropriate here because it helps convey the idea that the act of opening the door is similar to the act of allowing a breath of fresh air to enter one's world.
 
• It adds a sense of action and movement to the sentence, emphasizing the dynamic nature of the comparison.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Opening the door to her each morning is like **letting** a breath of fresh air into my world.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

An upright bar, post, or frame forming a support or barrier
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Stanchion**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let us look at the meaning of all the words: 
 
• **Repose **means a state of rest or peace.
 
 
• **Example**: "The cat was in repose on the couch."
 
 
 
• **Stanchion **means an upright bar, post, or frame forming a support or barrier.
 
 
• **Example**: "The stanchions held up the sign."
 
 
 
• **Recumbent **means lying down with the body supported on the back.
 
 
• **Example**: "The patient was recumbent in the bed."
 
 
 
• **Supine **means lying on the back with the face up.
 
 
• **Example**: "The doctor examined the patient in the supine position."
 
 
 
• From the meanings of all the words, it is clear that the best substitute of the words is "Stanchion".
 
• Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Shyam said, “My master is eating”

options.text: Shyam inform that his master is eating
Shyam say that his master is eating
Shyam and his master was eating
Shyam said that his master was eating

questions.solution: Option 1 is changing the tense and meaning both “inform” and “to say” are two different things. Secondly it should be “informed”. Option 2 again changes to present whereas it should be “said that” and not “say”. This makes option 4 as the correct choice. Option 3 is just rephrasing and not indirect. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Some girls were helping the wounded men.

options.text: The wounded men were helping some girls.
The wounded men were being helped by some girls.
The wounded men are being helped by some girls.
The wounded men received help from some girls.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The wounded men were being helped by some girls.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given **Active voice** is in **Past Continuous Tense.**
 
• Its structure is as follows: **Subject + was/were + (Verb+ing) + object.**
 
• While changing it into Indirect form, its tense will remain same.
 
• Its **Passive voice structure** will be: **Object(subjective case) + was/were + being + Verb₃ form + by + Subject(objective case).** 
 
 
• ​**Ex. Active: **Ram was playing cricket.
 
 

 **Passive:** Cricket was being played by Ram.

Hence, the correct answer is: The wounded men were being helped by some girls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Option 1 changes the meaning as if the wounded men were helping some girls. Hence, it is incorrect.
 
• Option 3 changes the context from past to present. Hence it is incorrect.
 
• Option 4 is in Simple Past tense. So, it is also incorrect.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Elated
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given word **'Elated' **is an adjective in English, which refers to being very happy and excited. (खुश)

 
 
• **For example, **She was elated at the news of her promotion.
 
 
 
• The correct answer **'Disheartened' **is also an adjective that refers to losing confidence or hope; discouraged. It is the opposite of elated. (निराश)
 
 
• **For example, **He was disheartened after the failure of his new venture.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is- **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Inspired'(Option 1) in English refers to being stimulated or motivated to do or feel something. It does not signify the opposite of 'Elated'. (प्रेरित)
 
• 'Cheered'(Option 2) in English refers to giving comfort or support to someone.
 
 
• It can be seen as similar in meaning to 'Elated' and not its opposite. (खुश किया)
 
 
 
• 'Encouraged' (Option 4) in English refers to inspiring someone with the courage or confidence to do something, not the opposite of 'Elated'. (प्रोत्साहित)
